target: Spoiler-free maximum verifiable archival completion of the original Mobage service

areas.name: Archival Service Route
areas.location_cue: The original handset or smartphone client, Mobage login, title screen, profile, collection album, and shutdown response.
areas.note: This is a terminated online service; completion is an evidence-preservation task rather than a currently playable routine.

save_backup.title: Duplicate client and account evidence first
save_backup.why: A launch attempt, migration, or expired login can erase the only surviving state.
save_backup.detail: Copy lawful application files and cached data, then record every accessible account screen before testing connectivity.

levels.1: The selected release depended on a Japanese social-game account.
levels.2: Use a lawfully preserved original client and account capture from the Mobage service.
levels.3: Verify the Japanese title screen, Mobage application identifier, device type, client files, account metadata, and dated service screens. No modern storefront, offline port, or verified complete emulator replaces the original route.

levels.1: One client family used Japanese carrier handsets.
levels.2: Document the docomo, au, or SoftBank build and Flash Lite 1.1 runtime.
levels.3: Record the handset model, carrier, firmware, browser, Flash runtime, application path, screen size, and input layout. Keep each carrier build separate because compatibility is not proven identical.

levels.1: A smartphone client supported early iOS devices.
levels.2: Document a surviving client compatible with iOS 4.1 or later.
levels.3: Record device model, operating-system version, application package metadata, account state, screen layout, and touch controls. Preserve the untouched package before attempting launch or migration.

levels.1: A second smartphone client supported early Android devices.
levels.2: Document a surviving client compatible with Android 2.2 or later.
levels.3: Record hardware, operating-system build, package identifier, files, account state, screen layout, and touch controls. Do not assume a modern Android compatibility layer reproduces the service accurately.

levels.1: The original servers are no longer operating.
levels.2: Treat June 30, 2015 as the end of normal service access.
levels.3: Preserve dated shutdown notices, connection errors, cached account pages, and original client data. Mark all server-dependent completion and limited rewards unavailable today unless a lawful complete preservation environment is demonstrated.

levels.1: Server-held collection data may exist only in old recordings.
levels.2: Preserve profile, squad, clan, card album, inventory, mission, and event screens.
levels.3: Capture every scrollable page from top to bottom with visible account identifiers redacted in the review copy. Keep the unedited private master, translations, timestamps, and navigation sequence together.

levels.1: Historical item purchases cannot restore a dead service.
levels.2: Do not spend money or use unofficial sales to imitate missing account content.
levels.3: Use lawful archived evidence only. Record historical paid-item existence as a verification hold, and never enter credentials, payment data, or unauthorized servers merely to fill a checklist slot.

areas.name: Verified Card and Clan Loop
areas.location_cue: Mission lists, battle screens, rescue results, card upgrade menus, squad formation, clan assistance, and the real-time clan map.
areas.note: Only public mechanical facts are exposed; identities and narrative context remain hidden.

save_backup.title: Preserve the collection before upgrades
save_backup.why: Strengthening, evolution, squad changes, and event claims may alter scarce account records.
save_backup.detail: Capture the full album and inventory before making any irreversible selection.

levels.1: Ordinary progression moves through short card-battle assignments.
levels.2: Open an available mission, form the requested squad, and complete its encounters.
levels.3: Record mission name only in the private spoiler-aware archive, then capture cost, squad, card attributes, battle steps, result, rewards, and the next unlocked screen. The complete mission list remains unverified.

levels.1: Limited assignments used separate reward structures.
levels.2: Open each preserved event page and complete every visible objective sheet.
levels.3: Record its availability window, route choices, task counters, hidden slots, ranking or clan conditions, claim buttons, and every reward. Expired events are archival records rather than obtainable modern requirements.

levels.1: A stage-ending encounter can award stronger equipment.
levels.2: Defeat the guardian displayed at the end of a mission stage.
levels.3: Capture the squad before battle, every card action, assistance, damage result, victory screen, and awarded weapon. Keep the opponent identity hidden in player-facing text.

levels.1: Some controlled units can join the collection after rescue.
levels.2: Complete the rescue interaction when a controlled unit appears during a mission.
levels.3: Record the encounter, rescue condition, success or failure, resulting card screen, attribute, rarity, and album change. Do not expose the rescued identity in the guide.

levels.1: Owned cards can improve without changing their record type.
levels.2: Open the strengthening screen and select only expendable materials.
levels.3: Back up the account evidence first, record base values, selected materials, cost, confirmation, gained levels, final values, and any cap message. Exact costs and caps remain unverified.

levels.1: A separate upgrade can change a card's form.
levels.2: Use the evolution screen only when all displayed requirements are met.
levels.3: Capture the original card, required duplicate or materials, cost, warning, confirmation, evolved art, attribute, rarity, values, and album entry. Preserve the pre-evolution state because reversal is not verified.

levels.1: Battle performance depends on the selected card group.
levels.2: Build a squad using the displayed attribute and formation rules.
levels.3: Record every slot, card attribute, values, equipment, total strength, formation bonuses, and saved result. The exact squad-size and optimization rules remain uncertain.

levels.1: Clan members can support a difficult group encounter.
levels.2: Request or answer clan assistance on an available guardian battle.
levels.3: Capture the request, participating members, time window, contributed damage, completion result, and individual versus clan rewards. Redact player identities from the public review copy.

levels.1: The competitive mode joins many players on each side.
levels.2: Enter a scheduled clan-versus-clan session with an archived eligible account.
levels.3: Record schedule, map, role, squad, action timing, assistance, scoring, result, standings, and rewards. Because service is terminated, preserve historical footage or screens rather than presenting the mode as currently available.

areas.name: Attributes and Rarities
areas.location_cue: The card detail page showing attribute icon, rarity mark, attack, defense, and upgrade state.
areas.note: Tier and attribute labels are neutralized to avoid exposing card identities.

save_backup.title: Capture unmodified examples
save_backup.why: Upgrade and evolution can change the only surviving card-detail evidence.
save_backup.detail: Record at least one untouched example of every documented attribute and rarity before altering it.

levels.1: Cards use a small set of battle specialties.
levels.2: Capture a card displaying the internal Power attribute in the private archive.
levels.3: Record its neutral album position, rarity, base attack, base defense, upgrade state, and squad interactions. Keep the attribute's identity-bearing card name outside player-facing text.

levels.1: Cards use a small set of battle specialties.
levels.2: Capture a card displaying the internal Speed attribute in the private archive.
levels.3: Record its neutral album position, rarity, base attack, base defense, upgrade state, and squad interactions. Keep the attribute's identity-bearing card name outside player-facing text.

levels.1: Cards use a small set of battle specialties.
levels.2: Capture a card displaying the internal Technical attribute in the private archive.
levels.3: Record its neutral album position, rarity, base attack, base defense, upgrade state, and squad interactions. Keep the attribute's identity-bearing card name outside player-facing text.

levels.1: The archive contains cards at several published rarity levels.
levels.2: Capture one card whose private record uses the Rare tier.
levels.3: Record acquisition context, album position, attribute, base values, upgrade state, and any event stamp. Do not assume the three documented tiers form the complete rarity table.

levels.1: The archive contains cards at several published rarity levels.
levels.2: Capture one card whose private record uses the Super Rare tier.
levels.3: Record acquisition context, album position, attribute, base values, upgrade state, and any event stamp. Do not assume the three documented tiers form the complete rarity table.

levels.2: Capture one card whose private record uses the Super Super Rare tier.
levels.3: Record acquisition context, album position, attribute, base values, upgrade state, and any event stamp. Do not assume the three documented tiers form the complete rarity table.

areas.name: Character Card Census
areas.location_cue: The character-card album, detail panel, attribute mark, rarity, values, and event stamp.

save_backup.title: Duplicate the album capture
save_backup.why: Many variants were event-limited and the server can no longer restore them.
save_backup.detail: Preserve the full scroll sequence and each surviving detail page before reconciling neutral record numbers.

areas.name: Final Archival Audit
areas.location_cue: The client archive, account capture, neutral card census, private identity map, event ledger, shutdown evidence, and verification holds.
areas.note: Completion is the maximum evidence-supported record of a terminated social game.

save_backup.title: Duplicate the reconciled archive
save_backup.why: Card variants and event records cannot be restored from the closed service.
save_backup.detail: Keep separate checked copies of the private research archive and spoiler-safe pack before final reconciliation.

levels.1: The archive must identify the exact client and account context.
levels.2: Confirm platform, client files, runtime, account evidence, shutdown status, and two backups.
levels.3: Compare device metadata, title and login screens, application package, dated account pages, connection response, and backup checksums. Reject unidentified recreations.

levels.1: Every verified system needs a complete evidence sequence.
levels.2: Confirm mission, event, guardian, rescue, strengthen, evolve, squad, assist, and clan-battle records.
levels.3: Review each sequence from entry through result, reward, and next state. Redact player and card identities only in the public review copy.

levels.1: Every documented neutral character record must map to private evidence.
levels.2: Confirm all character-card records against the spoiler-aware local census.
levels.3: Verify artwork, private name, variant, attribute, rarity, values, stamp, and acquisition evidence for each recovered record. Leave unproven routes marked uncertain.

levels.1: Every documented neutral creature record must map to private evidence.
levels.2: Confirm all creature-card records against the spoiler-aware local census.
levels.3: Verify artwork, private name, variant, attribute, rarity, values, stamp, and acquisition evidence for each recovered record. Keep identities out of player-facing text.

levels.1: Expired event families need dated objective and reward evidence.
levels.2: Confirm every represented event, subrequirement, reward page, and expiry notice.
levels.3: Check route choices, task sheets, login or exchange steps, clan conditions, rankings, manual claims, collaboration requirements, and unavailable status.

levels.1: No expired reward should appear as currently obtainable.
levels.2: Review every prerelease, code, login, anniversary, ranking, and collaboration item.
levels.3: Mark each historical window closed, distinguish account evidence from modern availability, and record any reward that required another service or physical product.

levels.1: Maximum verifiable completion must retain unknown live-service boundaries.
levels.2: Review every formal hold and attach corroborated evidence to any resolved entry.
levels.3: Leave unsupported holds uncertain. Replace one only when original documentation or a complete lawful account capture establishes the exact mechanic.

levels.1: The completed record is irreplaceable after service termination.
levels.2: Create two checked copies of client data, captures, translations, census files, and reports.
levels.3: Generate checksums, open representative files from each copy, store them separately, and retain a private identity-bearing research set plus a spoiler-safe publication set.
